NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's web site under City Council Meeting agendas at www.RollingHillsEstates.gov and
  during regular business hours in the office of the City Clerk. Meetings are live broadcast on the City's web
  site and a recording is available for viewing after each meeting. Meetings are also broadcast on PVP -TV
  Channel 35 (Cox) and Channel 39 (Verizon).

  Public Comment is welcome on any item during City Council consideration of the item. An opportunity is
  also provided for the public to comment on non-agenda items concerning City matters. If you would like to
  address the City Council regarding an item on this agenda or make a general public comment, please
  complete a speaker sheet and give to the City Clerk.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 24, 2024

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

MAYOR SCHMITZ called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by members of Happy Hoofers and the Palos Verdes Junior Drill Team.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Public Works Director David Wahba
  Community Development Director Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Assistant to the City Manager Jessica Slawson

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

None.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  STEGURA, TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-F AS FOLLOWS BY
  THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF SEPTEMBER 2024

  APPROVED WARRANTS 67776 THROUGH 67841 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $331,603.91, AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 080724; 090124
  THROUGH 090424; IN THE AMOUNT OF $138,561.59; FOR A GRAND
  TOTAL AMOUNT OF $487,508.50 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT AUGUST 2024

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

D.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT OF AUGUST 2024

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
SEPTEMBER 24, 2024
 E.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 10, 2024

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

F.  NOTICE OF COMPLETION - FOUNDERS PARK (PHASE 1) - KORMEX
  CONSTRUCTION, INC.

  1) ACCEPTED PHASE 1 OF FOUNDERS PARK COMPLETE, 2)
  AUTHORIZED THE CITY CLERK TO FILE THE NOTICE OF COMPLETION
  (NOC) WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY RECORDER’S OFFICE, AND 3)
  IF NO CLAIMS ARE FILED WITHIN 35 DAYS AFTER RECORDATION,
  DIRECTED STAFF TO RELEASE THE 5% CONSTRUCTION RETENTION
  PAYMENT TO KORMEX CONSTRUCTION, INC. IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $12,792.50.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT/PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

None.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

None.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  COST RECOVERY POLICY/ANNUAL UPDATE MECHANISM FOR THE USER FEE
  UPDATE - COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT AND PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENTS

  Recommendation: That the City Council review the draft cost recovery policy and
  annual update mechanism proposed for the Community Development and Public
  Works Departments, discuss the issues, and direct staff to return at the next regularly
  scheduled meeting with a recommended cost recovery policy, annual increase
  mechanism, and fee schedules for City Council consideration and adoption.

Community Development Director Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material).

Community Development Director Naughton explained the Planning fee schedule had not
been revisited in approximately 15 years, and the Building and Safety fees follow the
County’s fee schedule and are adopted by reference, which were last updated in 2015, in
response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF explained that residents have complained to her that permit fees
are too high and expressed concern about the annual increase mechanism as proposed.
Community Development Director Naughton explained that many Building Permit fees were
identified as too high and will be significantly reduced.

Community Development Director Naughton explained that the Community Services
department will also be analyzing its fees and will do a comprehensive user fee study later
this year, so this policy was written to be applicable for other departments to use as well, in
response to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN stated he supports the policy of recovering the City’s
overhead and thinks its good policy to use an unbiased outside resource to do the study.

MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA confirmed that once approved, the new fee schedule will be
available for the public on the City’s website.

Community Development Director Naughton explained that best practices for performing a
user fee study is to update every three to five years, in response to MAYOR SCHMITZ. She
further explained that because there is an annual increase mechanism within the policy, staff
thinks five years would be appropriate.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
SEPTEMBER 24, 2024
 Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  DIRECT STAFF TO RETURN WITH A RECOMMENDED COST RECOVERY
  POLICY, ANNUAL INCREASE MECHANISM, AND FEE SCHEDULES FOR
  CITY COUNCIL CONSIDERATION AND ADOPTION.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

B.  ROAD REPAIRS ON PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH, EAST OF ROLLING HILLS
  ROAD / WESTBOUND LANE. REQUEST TO AWARD A PUBLIC WORKS
  CONTRACT TO MENDOZA ENGINEERING COMPANY, INC.

  Recommendation: That the City Council award a Public Works Contract to Mendoza
  Engineering Company, Inc., in the amount of $65,619.50, plus a 20% contingency
  ($13,124) for a total of $78,743.50 to repair a portion of Palos Verdes Drive North
  (PVDN), including the adjacent walk path and curb and gutter, all located just east of
  Rolling Hills Rd. in the westbound lane.

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public Works Director Wahba explained the working hours for the project, including the traffic
control and construction noise, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER inquired about the impacts to the trail in this location. She
emphasized the importance of signage, and asked staff to inform the Palos Verdes Horseman’s
Association on the work that will be done.

Public Works Director Wahba discussed the 20% contingency, in response to MAYOR PRO
TEM STEGURA.

Discussion ensued about the bids received and the estimated line items of each bidder.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AWARD A PUBLIC WORKS CONTRACT TO MENDOZA ENGINEERING
  COMPANY, INC., IN THE AMOUNT OF $65,619.50, PLUS A 20%
  CONTINGENCY ($13,124) FOR A TOTAL OF $78,743.50 TO REPAIR A
  PORTION OF PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH (PVDN), INCLUDING THE
  ADJACENT WALK PATH AND CURB AND GUTTER, ALL LOCATED JUST
  EAST OF ROLLING HILLS RD. IN THE WESTBOUND LANE.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

C.  GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE POLICY REVIEW

  Recommendation: That the City Council review the draft Generative Artificial
  Intelligence (AI) Policy and provide direction to staff. Alternatively, if the policy meets
  City Council goals, it may choose to proceed with adoption.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
SEPTEMBER 24, 2024
 Assistant City Manager Davis noted that the policy covers legal compliance and copyright
concerns, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN commended staff for the well written policy.

MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA stated she was pleased to see the proposed policy includes
a human element to everything that is generated.

MAYOR SCHMITZ discussed generative AI and its widespread use.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  DIRECT STAFF TO PROCEED WITH ADOPTION OF THE PROPOSED
  GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) POLICY.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

D.  MASTER PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH CITYGREEN
  CONSULTING FOR SB 1383 COMPLIANCE REVIEW AND CITYGREEN CONNECT
  SOFTWARE SUBSCRIPTION

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve 1) Master Professional Services
  Agreement (MPSA) approved as to form by the City Attorney with CityGreen
  Consulting, and 2) Task Order 1-2024, under the MPSA in the not-to exceed amount
  of $20,000 for CityGreen Connect, compliance review and implementation record
  development, utilizing CalRecycle grant funds.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Assistant City Manager Davis explained that Waste Management will be an active partner
in this project, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  STEGURA, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE 1) MASTER PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT (MPSA)
  APPROVED AS TO FORM BY THE CITY ATTORNEY WITH CITYGREEN
  CONSULTING, AND 2) TASK ORDER 1-2024, UNDER THE MPSA IN THE
  NOT-TO EXCEED AMOUNT OF $20,000 FOR CITYGREEN CONNECT,
  COMPLIANCE REVIEW AND IMPLEMENTATION RECORD DEVELOPMENT,
  UTILIZING CALRECYCLE GRANT FUNDS.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

E.  SB 450 (ATKINS) VETO REQUEST LETTER- HOUSING DEVELOPMENT:
  APPROVALS

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the Mayor to sign and submit the
  letter requesting that the Governor veto SB 450.

Assistant to the City Manager Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
SEPTEMBER 24, 2024
 Assistant to the City Manager Slawson explained that the Governor will sign or veto bills on
his desk before the end of the month, and that staff will send the letter tomorrow, in response
to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AUTHORIZE THE MAYOR TO SIGN AND SUBMIT THE LETTER
  REQUESTING THAT THE GOVERNOR VETO SB 450.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  QUARTERLY 2024-2025 WORK PLAN UPDATE

  Recommendation: Receive and file.

City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  RECEIVE AND FILE.

MAYOR SCHMITZ so ordered.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF chaired the South Bay Cities Council of Governments’
(SBCCOG) Senior Working Group meeting this morning.

City Manager Grammer and Community Development Director Naughton highlighted that
the City of Rolling Hills Estates has been selected as one of the Institute of Local
Government’s (ILG) 2024 Beacon Spotlight Award Winners and will be receiving a Platinum
Level Award in recognition of our Community Greenhouse Gas Reductions and
Sustainability Best Practices, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER chaired the Equestrian Committee meeting last night.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN also congratulated staff on the ILG Beacon award and
noted that Assistant City Manager Davis is a finalist for the California Joint Powers Insurance
Authority’s (CJPIA) Capstone Award again this year.

MAYOR SCHMITZ attended the Los Angeles County Sanitation District meeting this month.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

MAYOR SCHMITZ thanked the community for attending the annual City Celebration on
September 14 and commended the City team for defeating Lomita Station in the annual City
vs. Sheriff volleyball game.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
SEPTEMBER 24, 2024
 13.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - ANTICIPATED LITIGATION Government
  Code Section 54956.9(d)(2)
  Significant exposure to litigation: one potential case

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 8:15 p.m. MAYOR SCHMITZ adjourned the meeting to in honor of Horrace Higgins who
turns 102 years old on October 9. The meeting was adjourned to Tuesday, October 8, 2024
at 7:00 p.m. for the purpose of a Regular meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit, City Clerk  Velveth Schmitz, Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
SEPTEMBER 24, 2024
